wallet_holds_erc20_balance.meaning: the builder wallet holds a nonzero ERC20 balance available to sweep

init_callable_by_any_caller.meaning: BuilderWallet.init() has no access control so any caller may invoke it

init_reinitializable.meaning: BuilderWallet.init() has no one-time guard and can be called again after initial setup

sweep_gated_solely_by_builder_admin.meaning: BuilderWallet.sweep(token,to) transfers the wallet's entire ERC20 balance to an arbitrary address and is gated solely by builderAdmin

sweep_authorized_by_legitimate_admin.meaning: the sweep call is authorized by the legitimate intended builderAdmin authority

erc20_theft_occurred.meaning: direct theft of ERC20 held by the builder wallet occurred (wallet balance transferred out to an unauthorized party)

assumptions: The builder wallet holds a nonzero ERC20 balance at the time of the sweep (report describes theft as potential).
The attacker is an unprivileged caller, not the legitimate builderAdmin.
Whether init() was previously called by a legitimate party is not stated; the plan covers both fresh and re-initialized wallets.

unresolved.description: Report does not specify concrete ERC20 token identities or balances held by builder wallets; theft is described as potential, so the balance is modeled symbolically.
Report does not state whether init() was already called by a legitimate party before the attack, so the pre-attack builderAdmin identity is not fixed.

limitations: Theft is formalized as the sweep transferring the wallet's ERC20 balance without authorization by the legitimate builderAdmin; the report does not give numeric amounts.
The authorization predicate is a report-grounded Boolean because the report states the gating condition qualitatively without a numeric definition.
Only the theft_erc20 impact is formalized here; other impacts are handled in separate claim-generation passes.
